Welcome to Langosphere

This short tour shows where everything is. In each step the bright, outlined area is the control being explained; everything else is dimmed. Use Next and Back, or Skip at any time. Any part can be repeated later from Settings ▸ Interactive tutorial.
The settings menu

Everything that applies to the whole app lives behind this button: the light / dark / system chips, the app language, the word limit for huge files, the file manager, the Theme section (full theme picker, accent and subtitle colours), the Prompts studio, the written App guide, this tutorial, the update check and About.
Tap the button to open the menu; closing the menu brings you back here.
The sections of the app

Reader, Video player, Online, AI and Leitner. Tap a tab, or swipe left and right across the page. Their order — and whether the bar sits at the top or the bottom — can be changed in Settings ▸ Theme ▸ Customize ▸ Layout & shapes.
Tap a tab to switch to it — the tour keeps running.
Tutorial language
The two chips at the bottom of this card switch the tutorial between Persian and English, on the spot, without touching the app language. The app language itself is in Settings ▸ App language.
Words and sentences

Everywhere in the app — the reader, the subtitle cards, the lessons — a tap on a word opens the dictionary popup (with pronunciation, I-know-this and Add to Leitner), and a tap on a sentence opens its lesson: meaning, grammar, structure, key words and examples. Words you save go to the Leitner tab.
Offline dictionary

Import a dictionary file here (MDX or SQLite). The popup only reads what is on the device, so with no dictionary a word tap shows nothing. Imported files are listed under the card and can be removed one by one, or all at once.
Tap Add dictionary to import a file now, if you have one.
Open a document
Tap here to load a text, PDF or EPUB file. Your reading position is remembered per file, and very large files are protected by the word limit in the settings menu, so the screen never freezes.
Tap here and pick a file — the tour continues by itself once it opens (or press Next to skip).
Document tools

Next to the title: import an AI lesson JSON made for this book, copy a page range to feed an AI chat, and the ⋮ menu with the comfort sheet, the chapter list for EPUBs and the page-image mode for PDFs.
Tap ⋮ to see the menu.
Reading comfort
Font size steps and the day / night paper live here. Line height, margins, warm tint and dimming are in the comfort sheet behind the ⋮ menu. This row appears once a document is open.
Tap A- / A+ or the moon to try them.
Fullscreen reading
Hides everything except the page. Tapping the page or pressing Back brings the normal layout back.
The page

Tap any word for the dictionary popup, with its sentence as context; tap a sentence for its lesson. Save words to the Leitner box straight from the popup. The AI tab can rewrite or correct this very text — it edits the same text you are reading.
Tap a word or a sentence to try the popups.
Import panel
Tap this header to fold or unfold the import drawer. It also folds by itself when you scroll down the subtitle list and opens again when you scroll back to the top, so the video gets the room.
Tap the header to fold and unfold the panel.
Video or audio file
The wide tile picks the media file. Audio files work too — the player then shows artwork instead of a picture. Your position in each file is remembered.
Tap it to pick a video or audio file now, if you like.
Original subtitle

The subtitle in the language you are learning. Pick a file from storage or paste a subtitle you copied; the chooser asks which. If it drifts, shift it by tenths of a second in the sync section of the player settings.
Tap it to see the file / paste chooser.
Translated subtitle
The same film in your language. Together with the original it builds the two-line view. Lines that have no translation yet can be translated one by one with the AI button on their card.
JSON learning package

The rich slot: besides the translation it carries the lesson, grammar, word list, pronunciation and examples for every line. It takes a .json file or a pasted AI answer; CHUNK 1-50 style answers are merged automatically, and the chunks panel lists, removes and exports them. The next steps open the Prompts window, where this package is made.
Tap it to see the file / paste chooser; Next opens the Prompts window.
The player

Tap the picture once to show or hide the controls; double-tap the left or right side to jump by the skip amount. The speed pill in the controls opens the study panel: speed, repeat this line, listen mode and coverage. Smart pause stops at the end of every line so you can read it.
Tap the picture to show the controls.
Video height
Drag this handle up or down to change how tall the video is compared to the subtitle list. The ratio is remembered.
Drag the handle up or down.
Subtitle cards

Every line is a card: tap a word for the dictionary, the line itself for its lesson, the speaker to hear it, and + to save the sentence to Leitner. The active card follows playback, and tapping a card seeks the video to that line.
Tap a word or a line to try the popups.
Tool cluster

The three dots unfold player settings (subtitle display, sync, smart pause, skip amount, audio track), A-B repeat, the subtitle switch, focus mode and fullscreen. A-B repeat: first tap marks the start, second the end, third turns the loop off. Focus mode hides everything except the video and the subtitles.
Tap the three dots to unfold the cluster.
The Prompts window

This is where the JSON learning package is made: a ready prompt for any AI chat, whose answer the app imports. Two families: Film subtitles — anchored to the video timeline, the one for the player — and Books & PDF, anchored to pages and paragraphs for the Reader. Keep Film subtitles selected.
Tap a family to compare them; the tour keeps Film subtitles.
Your learning level

A1 to C2. Every explanation, example and prompt in the app is tuned to this level — pick honestly: too high and the lessons skip what you need, too low and they bore you. This is your app-wide level; the prompt further down can use a different one.
Tap your level.
Dictionary or JSON lesson?

Once a line has a JSON lesson, tapping a word can open either the normal dictionary (switch on) or the lesson’s own explanation of that word (switch off). Off is the richer choice after your package is imported; on keeps the dictionary habit.
Flip the switch to read both descriptions.
How to use this — the five steps

The whole workflow, unfolded for you: 1) pick level and mode and copy the prompt; 2) open any AI chat (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini…), paste the prompt, then attach or paste your .srt file; 3) save the JSON answer as a .json file or copy it; 4) in the app: Video tab ▸ import drawer ▸ JSON slot ▸ select file or paste; 5) long films arrive in chunks — reply “continue” until the file is finished.
Six prompt modes

Each mode asks the AI for a different package. Translation only: line, timing, translation — fastest and cheapest. Translation + full lesson: the complete package the player is built around — the usual choice. Vocabulary & pronunciation: IPA, stress and fast-speech forms for listen mode. Grammar coach: one grammar point per line, explained and drilled. Leitner flashcards: only the words worth memorizing, as card fronts and backs. Single word analysis: one word and its sentence, for chat use — not an importable file.
Tap a mode card — the prompt text below changes with it.
From which language, to which?

Type the language you are learning (From) and your own language (To) exactly as you want them used; the prompt is rebuilt live and any pair works. The pills under the generator repeat what the prompt will say.
Edit a field and watch the pills change.
What the prompt will ask for
Three pills sum up the prompt before you copy it: From, To, and whether the answer is an Importable JSON (the five package modes) or For chat use (word analysis).
Prompt level

Starts at your own level but can be changed on its own — build an A2 package for a friend without touching your setting. It sets the vocabulary of the translations and the depth of the explanations the AI writes.
Tap a level chip.
Cues per request

A film has 800–1500 subtitle lines; no AI can write them all in one answer without being cut off. The prompt tells it to process this many cues, then stop and wait for the word “continue”. Every answer starts with a CHUNK 1-50 style marker and is a complete JSON on its own — the app recognises the marker and merges the chunks into one file. Smaller chunks never get truncated; 50 is a good default.
Tap a size.
Copy the prompt

One tap copies the whole prompt. Then: open an AI chat, paste it, send your .srt (attach the file or paste its text) and copy the JSON answer back. The prompt also tells the AI how to check its own answer: only JSON, strict syntax, every cue exactly once with its id, times in seconds.
Tap Copy prompt — you can paste it anywhere afterwards.
Read the prompt once

The text is unfolded below: the role and the level it writes for; the TASK (turn an .srt into a Langosphere JSON package, From → To); the RULES of the chosen mode; the JSON SCHEMA — the exact fields the app can import; the LONG FILES rules (chunks and the CHUNK marker); and the CHECK BEFORE YOU ANSWER list. Nothing needs editing, but reading it once makes the answers predictable.
Scroll through the text; it is selectable.
Back to the player

Close this window once the prompt is copied. In the Video tab, the JSON slot takes the file or the pasted answer; chunks arrive one after another and the chunks panel lists, removes and exports them. Next: the player itself.
Tap Close — the tour continues at the player.
Search

Type a channel name, or paste a YouTube video link, a channel link, an id or an @handle. A video link opens straight away. Nothing talks to Google directly: the tab streams through public Invidious and Piped instances, with no account.
Tap the field to type or paste a search.
Following and Saved
Following shows the latest uploads of the channels you follow; Saved keeps the clips you starred so they can be watched again offline.
Tap a tab to switch between them.
Channels

Tap a channel to see all of its videos, + to follow a new one, and long-press or Unfollow to drop it. The list starts with well-known English teachers (BBC Learning English, English with Lucy, Rachel’s English, …).
Tap a channel to open its videos, or + to follow one.
Instances

Which Invidious / Piped servers answer. Add your own, switch one off or move one to the top. If a clip refuses to play («sign in to confirm you’re not a bot»), that instance is being rate-limited — wait a few minutes or try another; playback also moves on to the next instance by itself.
Tap it to open the instance manager; Back returns.
Watch cache
The saving switch for all videos, the storage each clip holds and the default play / save quality.
Tap it to open the watch cache; Back returns.
Open a video

The cards are the videos of the channel, the search or the saved list. The small pill says whether an AI lesson is attached (Smart) or only raw captions are available, and ⋮ saves the clip or copies its link.
Tap any card to open it — the tour continues by itself in the player (or press Next to skip).
The online player

A clip opens in the same player as the Video tab: words, lessons, loops, speed, smart pause and focus mode all work here. The chip under the title switches between direct streams and the fallback web player when YouTube blocks a stream.
Tap the picture to show the controls.
Action drawer

Above the subtitle cards: the captions chip lists the video’s caption tracks (English loads by itself, a second track can be the translation line), export / copy puts the captions on the clipboard, in Downloads or in the Video tab, Attach JSON lesson adds an AI learning file to the clip, and the quality picker and the other player actions sit here too.
Tap the captions chip to see the tracks.
Tool cluster
The same three-dot cluster as the Video tab: player settings, A-B repeat, the subtitle switch, screen rotation, focus mode and fullscreen.
Tap the three dots to unfold the cluster.
Connection

This button opens the settings card. Fill in the base URL, the API key, the model name and your target language — any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. Nothing is uploaded anywhere except to that endpoint.
Tap the gear — the card opens below and the tour moves on.
The settings card

Base URL, API key, model and target language, plus the colours of the chat bubbles. The key is stored only on this device. A request that fails with an authentication or model error is not retried on purpose, so a broken key never costs you anything.
Memory
Opens the memory panel: prompts, corrections, skills and export / import — what the assistant has learned from you.
Tap it — the panel opens below and the tour moves on.
The memory panel

Prompts: every system prompt is editable, with the variables as chips, a reset button and a test run on three real lines. Corrections and skills: each translation you fix becomes a pattern sent along with future requests. Export / import moves the whole memory to a file — the safest way to another phone.
Tap the pills to switch between the four tabs.
Chat sessions
Conversations are saved as sessions, so you can leave one and come back to it later. The + button starts a fresh chat.
Tap it to see your sessions.
The conversation
The pills above show what the assistant can see right now: the loaded subtitles or the reader text. Answers that change a subtitle or the reader text are written straight back into the app.
Ask the assistant

Translate a subtitle, fix a translation, explain grammar or rewrite the reader text. Translation runs in batches with a cache, so identical lines are never paid for twice, and it can be stopped mid-run.
Tap the field to type a question.
Leitner box

The flashcards you saved from the word and sentence popups — this tab reviews and manages them. Five boxes: a correct answer moves a card up and brings it back later; a miss sends it down and brings it back sooner. The last box counts as mastered.
Quiz from JSON (beta)

Turns the imported AI learning file into a multiple-choice quiz on its words, sentences and grammar points. Pick a file or paste a raw AI answer, choose how many questions you want, and send every word you miss to the Leitner box with one tap.
Tap it to see the quiz card; the next step returns to the Leitner box.
Progress
The ring is the share of mastered cards; the text beside it counts the whole deck and the cards due today.
Export
Exports every card as an Anki-compatible file, so the deck can be used in Anki or kept as a backup.
Today or everything
Review today shows only the cards that are due; All cards lists the whole deck for browsing and deleting.
Tap a pill to switch.
Reviewing

Swipe left or right between the cards; tap a card to flip it in 3D and reveal the meaning — the answer buttons appear once it is face-up. The dots show the box level, and long definitions scroll inside the card.
Tap the card to flip it; swipe for the next one.
